description:
First real-hardware test of 05-12's promote/rollback mechanism (P23, P44 - both listed 'not yet done' in docs/probes.md). Constraint from this session's harness design: destructive operations may only touch &LIB (default <USER>2) and &LIB2 ('*B' => <USER>B) - <USER>1 must never be touched. 05-12's own actual promote step is CRTDUPOBJ FROMLIB(<USER>1) TOLIB(<USER>2), which this harness cannot run at all. So this manifest does NOT reproduce 05-12's literal walkthrough; instead it validates the underlying MECHANISM (CRTDUPOBJ across two real libraries, SAVOBJ/CRTSAVF/DSPSAVF, DSPOBJD DETAIL(*FULL) source-pointer evidence) entirely within &LIB/&LIB2, using &LIB as the 'production' role 05-12 gives <USER>2 and &LIB2 (<USER>B) doing double duty as both the SAVF/backup library 05-12 already gives it AND (only for this test) a stand-in second library to duplicate objects into/from, since a real second library besides <USER>1/<USER>2 is not available to this harness. TK0100D/TK0100 are recompiled fresh into &LIB from src/legacy/* (the as-shipped, pre-05-10 TANNM version - TXLEGACY's own version, matching part05-legacy-probe/part05-txlegacy-exec's already-confirmed compiles) for self-containment, independent of whatever TXMIGR TO(2) state (handled by a separate, parallel manifest) &LIB happens to be in; TANNM is irrelevant to the promote/rollback plumbing this manifest tests. Prerequisite: TXSETUP has already built the sample DB (TOKUIM/JUCHUM/JUCHUD/ZAIKOM/TANTOM) in &LIB, same standing prerequisite as every other part05-* manifest. No CALL of TK0100/JU0900C is attempted anywhere - 05-12's own real-hardware note already marks CALLing TK0100 (screen inquiry) as structurally V3/interactive, unreachable by this non-interactive-SSH harness; this manifest sticks to the DSPOBJD/DSPSAVF/QSYS2.OBJECT_STATISTICS evidence 05-12 itself relies on for confirmation instead. RTVCLSRC is exercised too (05-12's own third 'new' item), and now actually tests the safety net 05-12 describes rather than only the command's own syntax: right after CPJU0900C compiles JU0900C (ALWRTVSRC(*YES) explicit even though it is the default), RMVJUSRC deletes the JU0900C source member itself (&LIB/QCLSRC), then RTVSRC calls RTVCLSRC against the SAME member name (SRCMBR(JU0900C), not a side member like the earlier JU0900CR draft used) - this actually simulates 05-12's own stated scenario for this safety net ('ソース・メンバーを誤って消してしまった...場合'), rather than merely avoiding it. The earlier JU0900CR design had avoided the same member name because whether RTVCLSRC overwrites an existing member was unconfirmed; re-fetched ibm.com/docs/api/v1/content/ssw_ibm_i_75/cl/rtvclsrc.htm directly this session (2026-09-27) to settle it rather than leave it unconfirmed either way: its own text states 'If the member did not exist, it is created' AND 'If the member existed before the command was run, it is cleared before any source statements are written into it' - so RTVCLSRC would have safely overwritten JU0900C even without RMVJUSRC first. RMVJUSRC is kept anyway, not to dodge an unknown (there no longer is one) but because it is what makes this step actually test the lesson's own 'accidentally deleted' safety-net story instead of only testing RTVCLSRC's overwrite path. This is safe across connections because the 'file' step at the very top of this manifest re-sends and re-installs JU0900C's real source into &LIB/QCLSRC on every connection before anything else happens, so deleting it here never costs the next connection anything. VSRCJUC/CPJUSRC then copy the just-restored &LIB/QCLSRC(JU0900C) member into a dedicated single-member source file, &LIB/VFYCLSRC (RCDLEN 92, matching QCLSRC's own confirmed record length - tools/qclsrc/txlegacy.clp's own CRTSRCPF for QCLSRC uses RCDLEN(92) - deliberately NOT reusing part06-01-cvtrpgsrc's &LIB/VFYSRC, which holds RPGLE source at RCDLEN 112 in this same &LIB and whose SQL SELECT only reads its first member anyway), and the matching 'collect' (SELECT SRCDTA FROM &LIB/VFYCLSRC ORDER BY SRCSEQ) reads back real CL statement text (look for recognizable lines like 'CALL PGM(&LIB/ZA0500)') - not just 'the command didn't error' - to confirm RTVCLSRC actually recovered usable source, not an empty or garbled member. Unverified: whether CPYF between two source files of the same RCDLEN(92) but possibly different internal SRCDAT-format details needs FMTOPT - not expected to, but not confirmed either; and whether RTVCLSRC's own reformatting reproduces the source byte-for-byte (unconfirmed - only that recognizable CL statements should be legible either way). CRTSAVF/SAVOBJ/DSPSAVF/CRTDUPOBJ/DSPOBJD/RTVCLSRC/DLTLIB parameter syntax below was checked against IBM Docs (ibm.com/docs/api/v1/content/ssw_ibm_i_75/cl/{savobj,crtdupobj,rtvclsrc,dltlib,dspobjd,dspsavf,crtsavf}.htm, fetched 2026-09-27) before writing, per this session's own 'do not guess new CL syntax' rule - all of it matched or was a strict subset of what 05-12's own text already writes out, so nothing new was introduced by this fetch, only confirmation. RESTOBJ (05-12's own rollback step 15, 02-10's P23) is DELIBERATELY NOT attempted here: it is PUB400's own custom *CMD (not a real RSTOBJ/RSTLIB - IBM Docs has no page for it at all), its parameter names are documented nowhere in this repo (02-10's own text says 'F4 で開き、パラメーターを確認しながら' - i.e. even the lesson author never typed it non-interactively), and because every 'cl' step in this manifest is compiled into ONE shared CL wrapper program, a wrong guess at RESTOBJ's keywords would be a COMPILE-TIME error in that wrapper (unlike a wrong runtime value, which a MONMSG safely contains) - it would abort the wrapper's compile and lose the evidence for every other step in this same connection, exactly the risk this session's design instructions call out for untested CL/RPG syntax. So instead, the rollback half of this manifest is proven via CRTDUPOBJ alone: PROMDSPF/PROMPGM below put a real, directly-accessible (non-SAVF) known-good copy of TK0100D/TK0100 into &LIB2, and BREAKF/BREAKP/RESTF/RESTP later delete &LIB's copies and duplicate them straight back from that &LIB2 copy - proving the CRTDUPOBJ-based half of 'delete then restore' end to end, while the SAVOBJ/CRTSAVF/DSPSAVF half (real IBM Docs syntax, confirmed) is exercised in parallel as its own independent, unintegrated sub-test (BKUPSAVE/DSPSAVF01) so this connection ATTEMPTS to produce real backup-file evidence toward P23 even without RESTOBJ - see the DSPSAVF-evidence paragraph below for why 'attempts' rather than 'produces' is the honest framing here. Open question for the next connection (needs an interactive 5250/F4 session per 02-10's own instruction, not this SSH-only harness): RESTOBJ's actual parameter names, and thus the true SAVF->TMPxxxxxx->CRTDUPOBJ->DLTLIB round trip 05-12 steps 14-18 literally describe. TXPRDSP/TXPRDSP2 (DSPOBJD DETAIL(*FULL) OUTFILE dumps, one before CRTDUPOBJ and one after, both on the same &LIB/&LIB2 pair) exist specifically to answer P44 - whether CRTDUPOBJ's copy still reports its original compile-source location or the new library - collected below via 'SELECT *' rather than named columns, since this repo has not yet confirmed the *FULL outfile model's actual field names (same caution txmigr.clp's own header already applies to the *BASIC model). &LIB2's TK0100D/TK0100 duplicates (PROMDSPF/PROMPGM's output) are deleted again at the very end (CLNAFT1/CLNAFT2) so <USER>B is left holding only its proper role (the TXPRSAVF save file) - matching 01-04's own 'SAVF専用の置き場' description of <USER>B - while &LIB's TK0100D/TK0100 are deliberately left in their RESTF/RESTP-restored (rolled-back) state, matching 05-12's own cleanup instruction to leave <USER>2 in the post-rollback state.

DSPSAVF evidence capture (added after review; DSPSAVF01 previously had no evidence-collection step at all, only its CPF0000 MONMSG, which proves SAVOBJ/CRTSAVF did not escape but proves nothing about TXPRSAVF's actual contents): DSPSAVF01 now specifies OUTPUT(*PRINT) explicitly, matching this manifest's own DSPOBJD steps rather than silently relying on OUTPUT(*)'s default resolution. VSPLPF/CAPSAVF then attempt to materialize that print listing into &LIB/VFYSPL via CPYSPLF FILE(QSYSPRT) - QSYSPRT because it is the generic system printer file most CL commands' own *PRINT output resolves to when no other device file is named, which is well-known IBM i convention but NOT confirmed for DSPSAVF specifically - re-fetched ibm.com/docs/api/v1/content/ssw_ibm_i_75/cl/dspsavf.htm directly this session (2026-09-27) to check rather than take the reviewer's claim on faith: its own text for OUTPUT(*PRINT) says only 'The output is printed with the job's spooled output', naming no specific device/printer file at all, so QSYSPRT here is this manifest's own reasonable-but-unverified guess, not an IBM-Docs-confirmed fact. IMPORTANT CAVEAT, found by re-reading docs/probes.md before this fix (part06-0103-freeform, confirmed 2026-09-26, and re-confirmed by part06-01-cvtrpgsrc's/part06-1314-sql's own CPSPL/VFYSPL failures): a job invoked via this harness's own 'system "CALL PGM(...)"' mechanism (which is exactly how this manifest's CL wrapper itself runs) does NOT produce a real, CPYSPLF-retrievable spooled file when something in that job writes to QSYSPRT - the output instead flows directly into that system() call's own captured stdout, which run.mjs already saves verbatim as this connection's own 'run' section, with no extra step needed. That finding was established for a PROGRAM's own F-spec WRITE to QSYSPRT, not for a CL COMMAND's OUTPUT(*PRINT) resolving to QSYSPRT - which may or may not behave identically - so CAPSAVF (CPYSPLF) and the 'SELECT * FROM &LIB/VFYSPL' / default-query collect steps below are still worth trying (safe: CPYSPLF's MONMSG catches a wrong device-file name exactly like CPSPL's own precedent, and an empty VFYSPL costs nothing since it is not read as a hang signal). But the FIRST place to look for DSPSAVF01's actual printed listing, before concluding CAPSAVF/collect came back empty, is this connection's own result JSON 'run' section - not VFYLOG/the job log: 'run' is the raw captured stdout of the single qsh 'system "CALL PGM(...)"' invocation that runs this whole CL wrapper (per the already-confirmed pattern, that is where a QSYSPRT write actually surfaces), and it carries no step labels at all - so look there for recognizable saved-object names (TK0100/TK0100D/TXPRSAVF) or DSPSAVF-listing-shaped text, not for a 'DSPSAVF01' marker. Compile listings can also leak into 'run' the same way. VFYLOG (the wrapper's own job-log dump, read via the 'vfylog' section/the collect steps) is a DIFFERENT place - it only ever holds the SNDPGMMSG *INFO lines this wrapper itself sends (the 'XXX FAILED'/DONE markers), never a command's *PRINT listing, so DSPSAVF01's PASS/FAIL (did SAVOBJ/CRTSAVF/DSPSAVF itself escape) is what VFYLOG can confirm, while 'run' is where its actual printed content - if it appears anywhere in this harness at all - would show up. If DSPSAVF01's listing does show up in 'run', TXPRSAVF's actual saved-object listing (P23's real ask) is confirmed from that text directly, no CPYSPLF needed at all. QSYS2.OBJECT_STATISTICS's &LIB2 collect below now also selects OBJSIZE - confirmed as a real column via IBM Docs this session (WebFetch, 2026-09-27, ibm.com/docs/en/i/7.5?topic=services-object-statistics-table-function: 'OBJSIZE DECIMAL(15,0) Size of the object, in bytes'), not left as a guess the way SYSTABLES.JOURNALED was in 06-13/06-14's own first attempt (docs/probes.md, SQL42703) - as a second, weaker, independent signal: a non-trivial OBJSIZE on TXPRSAVF after BKUPSAVE is at least indirect evidence the SAVF is not empty, even if none of the print-listing capture paths pan out.

CPF4131 (record-format level-ID mismatch) scope note, added after review: 05-12's own text (the 'CRTDUPOBJ 対 再コンパイル' trade-off) calls out that CRTDUPOBJ cannot detect CPF4131 the way a recompile would, and this is the single most concrete, checkable claim in that trade-off discussion - but this manifest does not attempt to trigger or observe CPF4131 at all, and did not say so anywhere until this note. TK0100D/TK0100 are correctly NOT expected to hit it here (this manifest deliberately keeps &LIB/&LIB2's TK0100D format identical between the two libraries, matching 05-12's own 'today CRTDUPOBJ is fine' framing), so its absence here is by design, not a gap in THIS mechanism test. A dedicated CPF4131 sub-test (a small PF+RPG pair: compile against one field layout in &LIB, CRTDUPOBJ the program to &LIB2, recreate the PF in &LIB2 with a different field layout, ADDLIBLE &LIB2 POSITION(*FIRST), CALL the unqualified program name, expect CPF4131, MONMSG-guarded, placed last per this harness's hang-safety rule) was considered but deferred: it needs new, not-yet-written source and adds an OPM file-open failure path (RPG1216-class inquiry risk) to an already broad connection, for a claim that is orthogonal to what this manifest otherwise tests. It belongs in its own small, focused manifest (natural home: alongside part05-txmigr-to2, or a future dedicated 05-09 verification), not bolted onto this one.

steps.label: CPJU0900C
steps.cmd: CRTCLPGM PGM(&LIB/JU0900C) SRCFILE(&LIB/QCLSRC) SRCMBR(JU0900C) REPLACE(*YES) ALWRTVSRC(*YES)

steps.label: VSRCJUC
steps.cmd:
CHKOBJ OBJ(&LIB/VFYCLSRC) OBJTYPE(*FILE)
MONMSG MSGID(CPF9801) EXEC(CRTSRCPF FILE(&LIB/VFYCLSRC) RCDLEN(92) TEXT('verify harness RTVCLSRC recovered-source capture'))

steps.label: CPJUSRC
steps.cmd: CPYF FROMFILE(&LIB/QCLSRC) FROMMBR(JU0900C) TOFILE(&LIB/VFYCLSRC) TOMBR(JU0900C) MBROPT(*REPLACE)

steps.label: DSPB4DSPF
steps.cmd: DSPOBJD OBJ(&LIB/TK0100D) OBJTYPE(*FILE) DETAIL(*FULL) OUTPUT(*OUTFILE) OUTFILE(&LIB/TXPRDSP) OUTMBR(*FIRST *REPLACE)

steps.label: DSPB4PGM
steps.cmd: DSPOBJD OBJ(&LIB/TK0100) OBJTYPE(*PGM) DETAIL(*FULL) OUTPUT(*OUTFILE) OUTFILE(&LIB/TXPRDSP) OUTMBR(*FIRST *ADD)

steps.label: DSPAFDSPF
steps.cmd: DSPOBJD OBJ(&LIB2/TK0100D) OBJTYPE(*FILE) DETAIL(*FULL) OUTPUT(*OUTFILE) OUTFILE(&LIB/TXPRDSP2) OUTMBR(*FIRST *REPLACE)

steps.label: DSPAFPGM
steps.cmd: DSPOBJD OBJ(&LIB2/TK0100) OBJTYPE(*PGM) DETAIL(*FULL) OUTPUT(*OUTFILE) OUTFILE(&LIB/TXPRDSP2) OUTMBR(*FIRST *ADD)

steps.label: MKSAVF
steps.cmd: CRTSAVF FILE(&LIB2/TXPRSAVF) TEXT('verify harness 05-12 promote/rollback test SAVF')

steps.label: BKUPSAVE
steps.cmd: SAVOBJ OBJ(TK0100 TK0100D) LIB(&LIB) DEV(*SAVF) SAVF(&LIB2/TXPRSAVF) OBJTYPE(*ALL)

steps.label: VSPLPF
steps.cmd:
CHKOBJ OBJ(&LIB/VFYSPL) OBJTYPE(*FILE)
MONMSG MSGID(CPF9801) EXEC(CRTPF FILE(&LIB/VFYSPL) RCDLEN(133) TEXT('verify harness DSPSAVF spooled-file text capture'))

steps.label: CAPSAVF
steps.cmd: CPYSPLF FILE(QSYSPRT) TOFILE(&LIB/VFYSPL) SPLNBR(*LAST) JOB(*) CTLCHAR(*NONE) MBROPT(*ADD)

steps.sql: SELECT OBJNAME, OBJTYPE, OBJCREATED FROM TABLE(QSYS2.OBJECT_STATISTICS('&LIB', '*ALL')) X WHERE OBJNAME IN ('TK0100', 'TK0100D') ORDER BY OBJNAME
SELECT OBJNAME, OBJTYPE, OBJCREATED, OBJSIZE FROM TABLE(QSYS2.OBJECT_STATISTICS('&LIB2', '*ALL')) X WHERE OBJNAME IN ('TK0100', 'TK0100D', 'TXPRSAVF') ORDER BY OBJNAME
SELECT SRCDTA FROM &LIB/VFYCLSRC ORDER BY SRCSEQ
